display.title: Pirkei Avos, Chapter 1: What Moshe Learned from Mount Sinai
display.summary_short: Why the Mishnah says Moshe received the Torah 'from Sinai': he learned humility from the lowest mountain, the key to Ahavas Yisroel and achdus.
display.summary_long: A short Sefirah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains the custom of learning a chapter of Pirkei Avos each week between Pesach and Shavuos, and looks back at the first Mishnah of chapter 1: Moshe received the Torah from Sinai. The Mishnah says 'from Sinai' rather than 'on Sinai' because Moshe also learned something from the mountain itself. Hashem chose Har Sinai because it was the lowest mountain, a sign of humility. To serve Hashem truly we must be humble, see ourselves as lower than others and notice the good qualities in everyone, and follow them. Humility brings real Ahavas Yisroel and achdus, and then Hashem will turn the sad days of Sefirah into days of joy.
display.lesson: Be humble like Har Sinai and look for the good in every person; humility leads to Ahavas Yisroel and achdus.
